system:
You are the overnight interface designer in a certified adaptive EHR. Each night you redesign ONE clinician's UI program (JSON) so that tomorrow they spend fewer clicks, scrolls and mouse-travel pixels (keystrokes are secondary) on the same clinical work. The hospital's spec says what every workflow must capture and what must be shown before each commit. A Lean checker with a soundness proof certifies every version against the spec before it is deployed. Proposals that violate the spec are rejected, logged with a counterexample, and shown on a public dashboard, so propose changes you expect to pass and to reduce physical interactions for this specific user.

## UI program format
Lean types; JSON uses constructor-keyed objects ({"field": {"element": "...", "slot": "current", "prefill": "none"}}), nullary constructors are strings, and absent Option keys are omitted.
- Program { id, version, owner, role, specVersion, start, screens: Screen[], macros: Macro[] }
- Screen { id, title, workflow ("W1".."W7"), components: Component[] } (list order = render order)
- Component { id, kind, label, parent? (id of a group or tabs component on the same screen), tab (index under a tabs parent; tab 0 is open by default), visibility ("always" | {"unlessReceipt": {"info"}}), size ("normal" | "compact" | "tiny"), hotkey? (string), tag (stable semantic tag), copyOf? (id of the original when this is a copy) }. Keys marked ? are omitted when absent.
- Kind: "banner" | "tabs" | {"field": {element, slot: "current" | {"fixed": {"n"}}, prefill: "none" | {"fromRecord": {"fact"}} | {"default": {"value"}} | {"linked": {"element"}}}} | {"panel": {"info"}} | {"table": {"info"}} | {"trend": {"info"}} | {"alert": {"alert", "popup"}} | {"button": {"action": {"goto": {"screen"}} | "back" | {"commit": {"commit"}} | {"markReviewed": {"info"}} | "newOrderLine"}} | {"group": {"collapsible", "startCollapsed"}} | {"macro": {"id"}} | {"search": {"scope"}}. Vendor releases may add kinds; their JSON shape is shown when relevant.
- Macro { id, label, steps: ({"setValue": {"comp", "value"}} | {"click": {"comp"}} | {"goto": {"screen"}})[] }. A macro runs as the macro actor: it can never perform human-only steps or commits, and stops at the first one.

## Semantics that decide pass or fail
- "Shown" means: on the same screen, every ancestor group expanded (startCollapsed groups start closed), under a tabs parent only on tab 0, size not "tiny", and its visibility condition holds. Info in a closed group or an unopened tab is NOT shown.
- Review requirements: on each commit screen the required info must be shown. Only where the spec mode is shownOrReceipt may it be receipt-conditional: visibility {"unlessReceipt": {"info"}} hides it only while a valid receipt (same data version, inside the window, allowed role) exists. "shownOnCommit" info must always be shown on the commit screen.
- Human-only elements (spec humanOnly, identity, scan, cosign) and elements whose prefill policy is "never" are entered by a human every time: never pre-fill them and never set them from a macro.
- Pre-fill only as the policy allows: recordConfirm (from the record with provenance, human confirms), defaultConfirm (a default the human confirms), autoLinked (entered once, then linked).
- Units: weight is kg only; never source a value from a pound field.
- Enter once: no element may be asked twice on one path unless the later one is a pre-filled link or copy.
- Alerts: the interpreter opens condition-triggered interruptive alerts at the commit automatically, even when the component has popup=false. popup=true requests an immediate screen popup and is rejected for interruptive alerts by noFalseAlarms. Preserve certified interruptive alert components and their popup=false settings; passive alerts never pop up. Removable-tier alerts may be made passive or removed. Do not bundle unrelated safety or macro edits into workflow optimizations.
- Every commit stays reachable from the start screen, and every screen keeps the patient banner.
- Stability budget: at most N components may be moved (to a different screen, parent, or tab) per version. Copies (a new component with copyOf = the original's id) do not count, so prefer copying frequently used actions or info over moving them.
- Do not edit the program's id, version, owner, role, or specVersion; the loop sets them. The shared patientSelection binding is immutable and must remain enabled.

## Moves
Allowed (moveType): composeTaskView, copyToToolbar, reorder, merge, bringInfoForward, prefillWithProvenance, useReceipt, macro, defaultConfirm, shortcut, collapseOptional, surfaceFeature, migrate.
Forbidden: editing the spec, automating or pre-filling human-only steps, hiding required information, writing elements outside the spec, exceeding the budgets.

## Patch format
Each candidate is an RFC 6902 JSON Patch against the CURRENT program shown in the request. Address array elements by id or tag with selector segments, e.g. "/screens/[id=w1-sign]/components/[id=w1-sign-allergies]/visibility". "[id=X]+" is the position right after X (to insert after it) and "-" appends. Ops apply in order. Put each JSON value in "valueJson" as a JSON-encoded string (for example "\"compact\"" or "{\"id\":\"w1-tb-sign\", ...}"); use "" when the op takes no value. Use "from" only for move and copy ("" otherwise). New components need unique ids and every non-optional Component key; use "add" (not "replace") to set a key that may be absent.

## Predictions
"predicted" is your estimate of daily savings in clicks, scroll count, scrollPx and mouseTravelPx; keystrokes are secondary. Pixel values come from Chromium at 1440×900, component centers, straight-line travel and measured scroll offsets, with no tremor. Use null when geometry is unavailable. Improve at least one headline dimension, with no click/scroll-count regression and at most 2% + 1px regression in either pixel metric. Full completion is mandatory. Do not predict or optimize elapsed time.

response.hypothesis: P5 spends most physical effort navigating long screens: 1,667 scrolls and 388,018 mouse-travel pixels across four training days. W1 accounts for 38 of 44 tasks and averages 26.1 scrolls per task; its order composer uses normal-size controls throughout. Required review blocks remain displayed despite existing receipts, and removable reminders produced 12 popups. Compact controls, valid receipt-based visibility, and inline reminders offer distinct improvements without repeating the previously rejected navigation changes. Pixel savings require measurement.

candidates.summary: Reduce the vertical footprint of the frequently used clinic order composer.
candidates.rationale: W1 dominates P5's workload. Compact entry controls and their containers should reduce scrolling between medication details, dispensing details, and pharmacy confirmation. Every field, label, prefill policy, and navigation action remains available. This moves zero components.

candidates.summary: Present removable reminders inline without requesting immediate popups.
candidates.rationale: Training recorded 11 health-maintenance popups and one high-alert-order notice. Setting popup=false keeps these removable notices inline and should save dismissal clicks. This candidate contains only removable-alert presentation changes; all certified interruptive components retain popup=false. It moves zero components.

candidates.summary: Hide clinic signing review blocks while their permitted receipts remain valid.
candidates.rationale: P5 already created seven allergy receipts, seven medication receipts, and four CURES receipts. The three signing blocks currently remain always visible. Receipt-conditional visibility should reduce their vertical footprint without adding review clicks. The interpreter restores each block when its receipt expires, its data version changes, or its role is invalid. Order summaries, dose checks, and anticoagulants stay displayed. This moves zero components.
